डॉ. किरीट सोमैया : उपाध्यक्ष महोदय, आप सोचिए the TDS was used to be deducted at Rs 10,000. सीनियर सिटिजन बैंक इंटरेस्ट पर टीडीएस देते थे। इस बजट में उस इंटरेस्ट को दस हजार रुपये से बढ़ाकर उसे चालीस हजार रुपये कर दिया है। इससे कितना फायदा होगा? Now, what is the Budget? रिज़र्व बैंक ने .25 बीपीएस इंटरेस्ट रेट कर कम दिया है। इसका अर्थ यह है कि लाखों होम बायर्स को इससे फायदा हुआ है। अंत में मैं एक ही बात कहकर समाप्त करूंगा कि आज हिन्दुस्ता की साख और प्रतिष्ठा देश ही नहीं दुनिया में बढ़ी है। पिछले दिनों मैं और अनुराग सिंह ठाकुर जी डब्ल्यूटीओ की कांफ्रेंस में भाग लेने जेनेवा गए थे। वहां एक रेज़ोल्यूशन यूरोपियन यूनियन की ओर से लाया गया था। वह रेज़ोल्यूशन देखकर मुझे बहुत अभिमान हुआ। वे लोग कह रहे थे that we would like to stop India. India has become so much powerful that they are trying to block the transfer of technology. इसलिए मैं अंत में इतना ही कहूंगा कि आज एक ओर गरीबों के लिए लड़ने वाली सरकार है। मैं पीयूष गोयल जी, वित्त मंत्री का स्वागत करता हूं कि आपने एक बहुत बड़ा काम और किया है जो शारदा चिट फण्ड जैसी पोंजी, बोगस, बदमाश कम्पनियों के खिलाफ नया कानून बनाने का निर्णय लिया है। मैं उसका स्वागत करता हूं। इसी प्रकार से आप भारत के सवा सौ करोड़ लोगों के लिए अच्छा काम करते रहिए, यही मेरी शुभकामनाएं हैं। धन्यवाद।

*प्रो. चिंतामणि मालवीय (उज्जैन): स्वतंत्र भारत के ऐतिहासिक अंतरिम बजट पर चर्चा में अपनी बात रखते हुए मैं अपनी बात का प्रारंभ माननीय वित्त मंत्री जी के बजट भाषण के सेकंड लास्ट पेरे से करना चाहूँगा । माननीय वित्त मंत्री पीयूष गोयल जी ने कहा था कि यह सिर्फ अंतरिम बजट नहीं है बल्कि देश के विकास की विकास यात्रा का उत्सव है । यह जो देश बदल रहा है देश वासियों के जोश से बदल रहा है इसका श्रेय और यश उन्हीं को जाता है। हमारी सरकार में विकास को एक जन आंदोलन बनाया गया है।

उन्होंने संकल्प दर्शाया इन्हीं देशवासियों के बलबूते पर भारत को दुनिया का एक अग्रणी देश बनाएंगे, अभी नीव रखी है इस पर देश के सुन्दर भविष्य की इमारत रखेंगे ।

निश्चित रूप में जब बजट प्रस्तुत किया गया देश में उत्साही माहौल था सेंसेक्स 400 अंक तक उछल गया। किसानों, गरीबों व असंगठित क्षेत्र के मजदूरों में खुशी की लहर थी। जब माननीय प्रधानमंत्री नरेन्द्र मोदी जी ने सबसे पहले भाषण में यह कहा था कि मेरी सरकार देश के गरीबों, वंचितों, किसानों, मजदूरों की सरकार होगी । इस अंतरिम बजट में प्रधानमंत्री के उस वाक्य को पूर्णता प्रदान की है।

बजट में उन वर्गों की भी चिंता की गई है। जिनकी पिछली सरकारों में कोई पहचान ही नहीं हो सकी उनके वेलफेयर के लिए कोई प्रयास किया गया। देश में लाखों की संख्या में घुमन्तु जनजातियों के लोग हैं। ये पूरे देश में घूमते रहते हैं एक स्थान से दूसरे स्थान पर और अनिश्चित व सुविधाविहीन जीवन जीते हैं। उनके लिए भी एक नवीन घुमन्तु जनजाति बोर्ड का गठन वास्तव में अंतयोदय की समनव्यता का सही विस्तार देना है।

हिंदुस्तान की महिलाओं पर विकेंद्रित इतनी योजनाएं कभी किसी सरकार ने नहीं बनाई जितना माननीय प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी जी की सरकार में शुरू की गई। हिंदुस्तान की महिलाओं के लिए मोदी सरकार वरदान सिद्ध हुई है। ना केवल उसे भूख से मुक्ति मिली है, बल्कि उसे पैरों पर खड़ा करने के लिए मुद्रा ऋण योजना के 73% ऋण भी महिलाओं को दिए गए ।

श्रम मंत्री रहते हुए डॉ. बाबासाहेब आंबेडकर ने पुरुषों और महिलाओं के समान वेतन देने की व्यवस्था की थी लेकिन मातृत्व अवकाश केवल 6 सप्ताह का था जिसे माननीय प्रधानमंत्री मोदी जी की सरकार ने 12 सप्ताह किया था लेकिन उस मातृत्व अवकाश को भी 26 सप्ताह यानी 6 महीने कर देना निश्चित ही सरकार का क्रांतिकारी कदम है।

वर्षों से शौच के लिए बाहर अपमानित मैहरूम करती हमारी गरीब माताओं बहनों की पीड़ा पर कभी कांग्रेस की नजर नहीं पड़ी । इतने साल सरकार चलाने के बाद भी कभी इस तरह कोशिश नहीं की गई ।

यह आश्चर्य का विषय है कि अनेक पंचवर्षीय योजना बनाने वाली कांग्रेस की सरकारों ने किसी भी पंचवर्षीय योजना में 55 साल तक खुले में शौच से मुक्ति का कोई विचार नहीं किया गया ।

गरीब जो कांग्रेस का सबसे प्रिय विषय वस्तु है। लेकिन कांग्रेस ने गरीबी हटाओ का केवल नारा दिया कोई ठोस काम नहीं किया, योजना बनाई भी तो फूड सिक्योरिटी बिल और मनरेगा जैसी योजनाये जिससे गरीब जिंदा तो रहे लेकिन विकास न कर सके ।

कांग्रेस के शासन में समाजवादी और कम्युनिस्ट भी रोटी कपड़ा मकान शिक्षा स्वास्थ्य का नारा लगाते रहे हैं। समाजवादी धीरे-धीरे नमाजवादी हो गए और कम्युनिस्ट साम्यवादी नक्सलवादी बन गये। हजारों हत्या की लेकिन गरीब और गरीब हुआ लेकिन धरती पुत्र माननीय नरेंद्र मोदी जी ने गरीब की गरीबी हटाने के प्रयास किए 5 करोड़ गरीबों को प्रधानमंत्री आवास के रूप में पक्की छत दी गई, निशुल्क बिजली कनेक्शन दिए गए 700 जन औषधि केंद्र बनाए गए जहां गरीब और मध्यम वर्ग की को सस्ती दवाई उपलब्ध हो सकी। 17 हजार करोड़ रूपये उन्होंने गरीबों को सस्ते खाद्यान के लिए उपलब्ध करवाये ।

गरीब को जब कोई गंभीर बीमारी होती है तो उसका परिवार भी बर्बाद हो जाता है 4-5 लाख इलाज में लगाना मामूली बात है। बच्चों का स्कूल छूट जाता है, परिवार के गहने बिक जाते हैं, यहाँ तक की मकान भी रहन हो जाता है, फिर भी मरीज को बचाना मुश्किल हो जाता है। प्रधानमंत्री आयुष्मान योजना से देश के 10 करोड़ परिवारों को यानी 50 करोड़ लोगों को 5 लाख तक का इलाज का सुरक्षा कवच प्रदान किया है। जिसकी पूरे विश्व में कोई मिसाल नहीं है।

जब गरीब पर चर्चा होती थी तो सामान्यता आरक्षित वर्ग पर ही ध्यान दिया जाता था लेकिन एक वर्ग समाज का ऐसा भी है जो आरक्षित तो नहीं है। किन्तु गरीब है। जिस पर कभी कोई नीति नहीं बनाई गई। जिस पर कोई निरयोग्यता तो नहीं लादी गई लेकिन गरीबी स्वयं निरयोग्यता का बन गई और वह पिछड़ते चले गए मैं उन सामान्य वर्ग की बात कर रहा हूँ जो निर्धन है। उस निर्धन सामान्य वर्ग को भी 10% आरक्षण देने का ऐतिहासिक काम माननीय नरेंद्र मोदी जी की सरकार ने किया है।

न केवल गरीब लेकिन मध्यम वर्ग के लिए भी इस बजट में राहत दी है। मध्यम वर्ग की हमेशा यह शिकायत रहती थी कि सरकार हमारे लिए क्या करती है। हमारी हमेशा उपेक्षा ही होती है लेकिन आयकर की सीमा ढाई लाख से 5 लाख करके मोदी सरकार ने उसको भी एहसास करा दिया कि सरकार उनके हितों की चिंता करती है। राष्ट्र निर्माण में उनके योगदान को सम्मान करती है।

सामान्यता शिकायत रहती थी कि आयकर अधिकारी ज्यादा आयकर देने के लिए विवश करते हैं। रिटर्न की समीक्षा करते हैं लेकिन सरकार का आभार है कि जिसने निर्णय लिया कि अगले 2 वर्षों में 100 प्रतिशत आयकर रिटर्न कंप्यूटर से सत्यापित होगी और किसी इंस्पेक्टर की कोई भूमिका नहीं होगी ।

यद्यपि कांग्रेस ने सदन में जीएसटी का समर्थन किया। जीएसटी कौंसिल में भी राज्य सरकारों के मुख्यमंत्री और वित्त मंत्री होते और निर्णयों में साझीदार भी होते हैं। लेकिन यह कांग्रेस अध्यक्ष का दोमुहापन है कि संसद से बाहर आकर गब्बरसिंह टैक्स कहकर आलोचना करते हैं।

एक देश एक टैक्स की इस कर व्यवस्था ने देश को एक साझा बाजार दिया है। व्यापार-व्यवसाय आराम हुआ है कर प्रदाता आई है। लेकिन कांग्रेस ने गैर जिम्मेदार रवैया अपनाते हुए असंतोष भड़काने का काम किया है।

छोटे कारोबारियों को जीएसटी से छूट 20 लाख से 40 लाख करने व 3 महीने में एक बार रिटर्न भरने की अनुमति के लिए भी मैं सरकार का आभार व्यक्त करता हूँ। डेढ़ करोड़ तक टर्नओवर वाले व्यापारियों को 1 प्रतिशत निर्धारित जीएसटी देने के निर्णय से व्यापारी बहुत प्रसन्न है। और यह व्यापारियों की लंबे समय की मांग थी जो आज 90 प्रतिशत व्यापारी इन्हीं दो श्रेणियों में आते हैं। कुल मिलाकर यह बजट अन्तोदय की व्यवहारिक परिणति के साथ मजबूत अर्थव्यवस्था का आधार बनेगा । मैं माननीय वित्त मंत्री और सरकार को धन्यवाद और आभार करते बजट का समर्थन करता हूँ।

*DR. B.K. BIJU (ALATHUR): Thank you for giving me the opportunity to speak on the Interim Budget 2019 presented by the Interim Finance Minster, Puyush Goyal Ji.

At the outset, the Narendra Modi Government has broken with over 70 years of Parliamentary convention and used an " interim" Budget to harvest votes in the general election. The Budget speech is nothing but an election stunt listing out imaginary achievements of the Government during their tenure. The Finance Minister's theatrical speech in Lok Sabha has evaded practically all the important problems, such as the agrarian crisis, unemployment and break down of education and healthcare systems. 

I have no hesitation to call this Government a regime of manipulation. In January 2015, Narendra Modi Government revised the base year of national income estimates from 2004-05 to 2011-12. It was not merely a change in the base year, but also a complete revamp in the methodology of calculating India's Gross Domestic Product (GDP). Ordinarily, revised methodologies are detailed in extensive documents released by the CSO, but no such document has been released in this case. And the claims of higher GDP growth are not reflected by ground realities. If growth is high, companies should be out there, recruiting. Where is any recruitment happening now?

On the macroeconomic front, when the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) came into power in 2014, the GDP growth rate was at 7.4%. In 2015, the GDP growth rate was at the rate of 8.2%. However, there was a dip in the GDP growth rate in 2016 and 2017, i.e. 7.1% and 6.7% respectively, as a result of demonetization shock and the hasty introduction of Goods and Services Tax (GST) in the economy. 

Why the Government is playing with the date? The answer is very clear. They have to cover up the consequences of draconian demonetization and the flawed tax reform measures. There is a complete status quo in fiscal consolidation. The Government hopes to contain the fiscal deficit in 2018-19 at 3.4% of GDP and has projected an identical number for 2019-20. The figures available for April-November show that gross revenues from Central taxes in 2018-19 increased by barely 7.1% per cent over the same period in the previous year. However, the revised estimates for 2018-19 show an estimated 17 per cent growth in revenues over actuals for 2017-18! Even after this, revenues are slotted to be Rs. 23,067 crores less than the Budget Estimates announced a year ago. In a repeat of what it did last year, the Government has put inflated revenue figures for both income tax as well as GST Revenues. Interestingly the lower than budgeted collections of GST in 2018-19 by almost Rs. 1 lakh crore is supposed to be covered by higher collections from Corporation Tax and Customs duty leaving a shortfall in tax revenues of just about Rs. 23,000 crore. How realistic are the projections for 2019-20? 

Our Primer Minister is a Pied Piper of Hamelin. The goodies given to the poor farmers proved it. Budget Friday, said farmers will be provided Rs. 6,000 per year, which amounts to Rs. 16.44 daily, in three installments under Central Government Scheme. It adds insult to injury to the plight of the poor farmer. Agriculture has become a death game for the poor farmers in our country. The absence of supporting system from the Government such as subsidies, credit etc.. has pushed more than 3 lakh farmers into suicides. As per the latest 2015-16 Agricultural Census, there are about 12.56 crore small and marginal farmers in the country, making up 86% of all farmers. It will imply an expenditure of at least Rs. 75,000 crore and the Government is maintaining a studied silence on where this huge amount is going to come from this, its implementation is a puzzling question. It will fraught with uncertinty because land titles will need to be checked, lists made and so on. 

Taking a cue from the past experiences, it is typical of Modi Government to sell dreams to the poor-only dreams. Again the landless farmers and agricultural workers are excluded from this budget. Take the example of another Scheme, the much-touted Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) started in 2016. Astonishingly, many fundamental problems and issues remained almost the same in both the old crop insurance schemes and also the new PMFBY. CAG has spotted huge gaps in PMs Fasal Bima Yojana and other crop insurance schemes. With just 45% of all claims made under PMFBY paid so far, the scheme is a huge failure. The corruption involved is bigger that the Rafale scam. While Rupees 10 lakh crore of corporate debts have been written off, only 10% of farmers gain from loan waivers. The Government is standing with whom? Farmers or Corporates. 

Modi Magic has no limit. The 7.5 percent hike in subsidies for food, fertilizers and petroleum is also hiding the facts. According to the 15 percentage Subsidies announced last year for food, fertilizers and petroleum, there is a cut of rupees 1000 crore for food and 4413 crore for fertilizer in the current budget. Having been directly responsible for aggravating agrarian distress which has destroyed farmers' incomes by much more than that, the Government is covering up for the betrayal so its promise of a MSP one and a half times the production costs. Again no change in subsidized rates food grains was announced. 

It is not a Make in India, it is Selling India. Modi Government has a penchant for selling our PSUs. The 235 public sector undertakings that were once the commanding heights of India's socialistic economy and still account for about 20 per cent of the GDP and 15 per cent of stock market capitalization through 50 listed firms. This has helped us to withstand the perils of the latest Global economic crisis. Dismantling the public sector became a part of the Government agenda since 1991 with the official advent of neoliberal policies under the Congress Government. The Modi Government has intensified these policies. Modi Government has decided to shut down 15 loss-making Public Sector Undertakings which had been identified by NITI Aayog for closure. Another 74 has been in waiting list. On the other side, the decision of the BJP led Government to allow 100% Foreign Direct Investment is such strategic sectors of our economy like defence, railways, telecom, civil aviation, satellites, power petroleum, mining, coal etc is nothing but anti national in character. 

MSMEs is another sector neglected by the Budget 2019 which has borne the maximum brunt of demonetisation misadventure and sub-optimal GST implementation. Apart from the scheme of sanctioning loans up to Rs. 1 crore within 59 minutes which was announced by the PM earlier, 2 % interest rate rebate in incremental loans, increase in the priority sourcing of SMEs to 25% by public enterprises with 3% reserved for women entrepreneurs, there is not much to appease the sector. 

Here is another Modi Joke-Giving pension to the worker after 32 years. More than 82 percent of the workforce is employed in the unorganised sector in India, as noted by the International Labour Union. There is estimated 40 crore workers in this sector. Pradhan Mantri Shram-Yogi Mandhan promises a pension of a mealy Rs. 3000 a month after 32 years of a person contributing Rupees 100 every month. What does this say about? What is the economic status the Modi Government expects the supposed beneficiaries to have after more than three decades? And what does the Government have to commit itself today to this great 'promise'? A paltry Rupees 500 crore have been allocated for this scheme which won't even begin to cover a fraction of the estimated 40 crore workers is another cruel joke of the NDA Government. The average life expectancy of an Indian is 68. Again, a causal worker who works under precarious conditions will have an average life expectancy much lesser than that. How many would be alive to receive the Governments pension after 32 years. 

Unemployment is an issue that the goebbelsian propaganda makers are hiding under the blanket. More than half of the working age population is out of the Labour force in India. The Government is hiding this real picture by withholding official data. Two independent members of the National statistical Commission, which prepared the study resigned in January 2019, reportedly in protest against the Government for not publishing the employment status report. A Government that promised two crore new job in that time, and the Prime Minister has been reduced to claiming that pakoda-sellers on sidewalks should also be counted in the employment figures. Analysts now have to rely on private sources and indirect evidence to understand the real situation. According to the leaked data of NSSO for 2017-18 unemployment peaked to 6.1 per cent, at high level in the last 45 years. Labour force participation declined from 39.5 percent in 2011-12 to 36.9 per cent in 2017-18 and youth unemployment rate has climbed steeply: 18 percent for urban male and 27 per cent for urban female the first full year after demonetisation. The CMIE data has shown a loss of 11 million jobs during 2018. Who is responsible for this?

An example of the Modi Government's duplicity is visible in the allocation of the much-publicized Beti Bachao Beti Padhao programme. Funds for this programme have been cut from an already embarrassing Rs. 255.9 crore to just Rs. 100 crore. The important Mid-Day meal Scheme has seen an increase of just Rs. 51 (0.005%) compared with last year's expenditure. In real this means an actual decline, harming crores of school going children.

Interestingly, despite the Government's repeated claim on its stress on improving higher education, the allocation for Higher Education Financing agency (HEFA) has been reduced from Rs. 2,750 crore last year to Rs. 2,100 crore this year. The actual spend by HEFA last year was just Rs. 250 crore. In the last four years, seven IITs, seven IIMs, fourteen IIITs, 15 AIIMs, one NIT, and four NIDs have been set up or are in the process of being set up. But most of them are get to be functional and suffer from shortage of faculty. The total allocation for all the Central Universities put together has been nominally increased by only about 1.6% again an increment that is washed out by inflation. Funding for the University Grants Commission is a prelude to the privatization of higher education. It has also been reduced from rupees 4687.23 crore in 2018 to rupees 4600.66 crore in 2019. A combined allocation of Rs. 14,697 crore has been made to two science ministries in the 2019-20 interim Budget, recording a marginal hike from last years' allotment, figures suggest. Prime Minister Narendra Modi had vowed to put an Indian in space by 2022. India's first manned space flight, Gaganyaan, will send three humans into space for five to seven days. But here is a cut of rupees 550 crore for the space research. Marginalization of social science research is the other side of the story. While technical and management institutions such as IITs, IIMs etc. are provided funds on a platter, through cutting allocation for Higher education, the Government is clipping the wings of Social Science research. 

It is a fact that Indian health sector too is on the path of complete privatization under the Modi Government. Ayushman Bharat Scheme is one of the most celebrated healthcare initiatives of the Government, which is meant to provide Rs. 5 lakh insurance cover to 10 crore families. The relentless drive towards privatisation of public health systems in the country has only just begun with Ayushman Bharat. Modi said it was "an opportunity to serve the poor" and to "empower the poor". But experts, evidence, and past experience with insurance schemes in the country tell a different story. Besides paying for the premiums to be share 60:40 between Centre and states, except for the Northeastern States and the three Himalayan States of Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal and Uttarakhand, this allocation will be used to cover the costs for setting up the technology to go with it; the National Health Stack,, a complicated digital infrastructure to subsume all medical and healthcare activities in the country, with the primary aim of enabling private players to harvest the health data of citizens. The Government will pay the premium for the insurance cover given to the people by private insurance companies, whose entry is also facilitated by this scheme. Besides that allocation for it has been earmarked at a measly Rs. 6,400 crore this year. How this scheme can be rolled out with this amount is anybody's guess. Apart from budget deficiencies, the Indian system is also suffering from the deficiencies of infrastructure and doctors. Limited doctors mean limited facilities, which are insufficient to serve our population. The already insufficient infrastructure appears to be more inefficient with the increasing incidence of non-communicable diseases, such as diabetes, cardiovascular diseases, stroke, cancer, etc. another crucial head under which allocation has been cut is of upgrading district hospitals. Allocation has gone down from Rs. 3,168 crore to just Rs. 2,000 crore. This will force people towards private hospitals. 

The pictures of the flagship hare -brained schemes are not different. Almost all the schemes aiming the social empowerment of the poor masses especially in the rural areas are deeply neglected in the budget. The much coveted rural jobs guarantee scheme, Mahatama Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act is providing some relief to the rural poor in the form of employment Guarantee Act is providing some relief to the rural poor in the form of employment and social security. Interim Finance Minister has allocated Rs. 60,000 crore to MGNREGA, which seems huge. However, the allocation for MGNREGS as a percentage of national income decreased form 0.33 per cent in 2011-12 to 0.26 per cent in 2017-18. Similarly, the social assistance programmed (NSAP) which included old age and widow pensions suffered a cut of rupees 775 crore in this budget. 

What is the attitude of the Government towards SC/STs? Dalits and Minorities are social segment worst hit by the policies of the NDA Government. Certain programmes were initiated decades ago to enable these communities to "catch-up" with other sections of society in terms of their level of material development. Two such programmes are the Tribal Sub Plan (TSP) for STs which was started in 1974, and the Special Component Plan (SCP) for SCs which was initiated in 1979. As part of these programmes, funds in proportion to the population shares of the SCs and STs were to be allocated by the Government while formulating the Budget. Under the Modi Government. The Special Component Plan for SCs and the Tribal Sub Plan has been downgraded to mere schemes for the welfare of SCs and STs and has been left hanging without any clear guidelines being issued. A drastic change in the Scheduled Castes Sub Plan (SCSP) and Tribal Sub Plan (TSP) component of the Budget, which have been replaced by 'allocations for welfare of Scheduled Castes', under statement 10A, and 'allocations for welfare of Scheduled Tribes', statement 10 B. Now funds are given to various Ministries. As a consequence, a large proportion of funds for the SCs and STs with various ministries remain unspent. Central scholarships for SC/STs has been reduced from rupees 500 crore in 2018 to rupees 390.5 crore. The umbrella scheme for Dalits, comprising scholarships, financing for jobs etc. suffered a massive cut of over 30% from the current year's revised estimate. Central Scholarships for higher education for Dalit students too suffered a cut from previous year's Budget allocation. This shows the extent of concern that the Modi Government has for Dalit communities. The budget for minorities remains static as last year at Rs. 4700 crore. 

With tax soaps the Government is fooling the middle class also. It is not the exemption limit which has been raised but the tax rebate under Section 87A of the Income Tax Act which earlier provided a rebate of Rs. 2,500 for those with net taxable income up to Rs. 3.5 lakh. The tax rebate given to taxpayers is expected to cost the exchequer Rs. 20,000 crore. Since it is a rebate rather than an increase in the exemption limit will disappoint many tax payers who were hoping for indexation of the threshold and get relief. However after the euphoria, the reality check is likely to disappoint many. 

It is a " ACHHE DIN" for corporate. Diversion of funds in the name of banking recapitalisation is another tricky game of the NDA Government in favour of the corporates. In reality all the banks are under debt crisis due to the Non-Performing Assets. Some of the country's biggest banks are reporting losses with lakhs of crores gross Non-Performing Assets (NPAs) amounting to about 5% of the country's GDP. These has caused due to the non-payment of loans givern to the corporates . Last year 5 lakh crore rupees have been earmarked for banking recapitalisation. This year it has crossed 10 lakh crore. This banking recapitalisation would be done by diverting funds from the social welfare sectors. While the Government cutting funds from social welfare sector, funds are being served to the corporates on a platter. While appeasing the Corporates without any checks and balances, the Government seemed to be scraping the bottom of the barrel by asking the RBI to transfer a surplus of Rs. 3.6 lakh crore, more than a third of the total Rs. 9.59 lakh lakh crore reserves of the central bank, to the Government. It is the first case in the history of 43 years; the Reserve Bank Governor of India has been resigned owing to increasing tensions between the Finance ministry and the Reserve Bank of India. It is a shame on the Modi Government. 

Even if the BJP-led NDA Government presented the interim budget eyeing the upcoming Parliament elections, kerala was not given enough consideration. Kerala has witnessed the biggest flood this season since 1924. Ten of its total fourteen districts have been severely affected. 27 Dams have had to be opened. From August 9 to 12, 39 people have died, and the overall death toll stands at 186 in this season. More than 60,000 people have been housed on various relief camps across the state and 211 places have seen landslides and landslips. Around 20,000 houses have been destroyed, and nearly 10,000 km of public roads have been damaged. No package was announced in the budget for the state to tide over the August deluge and to strengthen its rebuilding initiatives. 

The budget, which reduced the existing allocations to the states, was silent about many long-pending demands of Kerala. Kerala has been a historically neglected region for railway. The insufficient funds earmarked for new lanes, gauge conversion, doubling of lanes and electrification act as a major impediment of the railway development of the State. The long-standing demand of the State for more trains from important cities, a separate railway zone, track doubling and electrification, development of adarsh stations at Mulamkunnathukavu, Vallatholnagar and vadakkancherry, has not been met. Kerala has acquired 235 acres of land for the Kanjikkode factory. Even after laying the foundation stone before six years, nothing has been done on that land. Declaration of Minimum Support Price for cash crops is the only way out to save the farmers from committing suicides. The demand for increase in import duty for rubber is a long pending of demand of Kerala. Many other demands of Kerala have been yet to be fulfilled such as increasing the amount of financial assistance to IAY programme. Demand for an AIIMS and development of the IIT at Palakkadu is still remained as a distant dream.

I strongly oppose the interim Budget 2019-20 since it is yet another eyewash of the Modi Government. Through manipulated and inflated data, it hides the grim realities on the ground and this Government is another example of how crony capitalism could worsen the misery of the common man.
